title: Seller Acceleration Atelier — Playbook (Draft)
content:
Purpose and elevator
- One-line: a compact, repeatable 90–120 minute hands-on 'atelier' for SEs + platform engineers to convert pilot conversations into production-ready engagements.
- Why different: mixes field roleplay, live canary scripting, and a short economics sim so sellers can close with operational confidence (latency, cost, fallback).

Slide 1 — Agenda (90m atelier)
- 0–10m: Context + goals (seller, eng, ops outcomes)
- 10–35m: Quick technical primer + model/latency/cost cheat sheet
- 35–65m: Roleplay: pilot qualification + escalation simulation (two 15m rounds)
- 65–85m: Canary runbook workshop (write & test a minimal canary)
- 85–90m: Commitments and next steps (pilot owner, success metrics)

Slide 2 — Intended outcomes (what leaders care about)
- For SEs: high-confidence pilot checklist + two fallback scripts that reduce pilot churn by 40% (goal)
- For Platform Eng: a canary template that maps to Dedicated/Hosted and the exact SLO targets to propose in contract term sheets
- For Customer: clear rollback & cost-visibility plan tied to pilot KPIs

Slide 3 — Quick primers (one-pagers to hand out in session)
- Model variants table: latency/quality/cost per 1k tokens (hosted vs dedicated vs quantized-proxy)
- Routing policy decisions: when to prefer region vs cost tier vs latency tier
- Prefix caching & batching impact: sample numbers (20%–60% token cost reduction depending on workload)

Slide 4 — Roleplay script (Round A: qualification)
- Persona: Senior Platform Engineer (customer) — concern: unpredictable tail latency under concurrency
- SE playbook bullets: ask for 95/99th p99 tail context, ask about request burst patterns, offer a pilot plan: small sandbox with synthetic replay + canary 1:1 map to production traffic
- Signals to push: controlled commit (reserved capacity) vs flexible (hosted) — tradeoffs phrased in ops terms

Slide 5 — Roleplay script (Round B: crisis + fallback)
- Scenario: pilot sees spike in longer contexts; p99 doubles in week 2
- SE to Platform Eng: propose immediate tactical fallbacks: switch to compatible model variant, auto-fallback region, and a temporary sequence-length limit with graceful notify
- Acceptance criteria: p95 within SLA, and cost delta < 2x baseline for the week

Slide 6 — Canary runbook template (hands-on)
- Minimal canary checklist (1 page): traffic subset selection, metric mix (latency p95/p99, error rate, cost per 1k tokens, quality sample set), rollback criteria, duration (48h typical)
- Live task: fill the template for a sample customer (we'll run with synthetic replay of 1k reqs to mimic expected burst)

Slide 7 — Canary config example (sample values)
- Traffic slice: 2% of authenticated traffic, same client ID, mixed prompt lengths (20% short <128, 60% med 128–512, 20% long >512)
- SLOs: p95 < 400ms, p99 < 900ms for med-only; error rate < 0.1%
- Fallback policy: immediate model-variant switch on sustained 3m p99 > 1.5x target

Slide 8 — Economics micro-sim (2-minute calculator)
- Inputs we collect live: avg tokens per request, calls/day, desired replication factor, region egress estimates
- Quick rule-of-thumb outputs: expected $/month hosted vs dedicated vs hybrid (with quantization) and a one-line talking point for CFO: "expected unit cost reduction of ~X% if we enable prefix caching + 8-bit quantization"

Slide 9 — Troubleshooting cheat sheet (top 6 fixes)
- 1) High cold-start p99: look at batch sizing & warm pool config. Quick mitigation: add warm replicas (10–20m).
- 2) Unexpected errors on long contexts: enforce truncation guard rails at client side for pilot run.
- 3) Quality regression after quantization: toggle to float fallback variant + tag eval set; initiate rapid eval.
- 4) Cost spikes: check caching hit rates and reroute infrequent heavy prompts to dedicated short-term bucket.
- 5) Authentication throttling: confirm token limits & retry windows.
- 6) Observability blind spots: add per-route tracing with a single opaque id map for root-cause.

Slide 10 — Seller speaking bullets (30s soundbites)
- "We design pilots so we know exactly what failure looks like — and how to fix it before it hits your customers."
- "If you need predictable throughput, we map the pilot to reserved capacity with a rollback leash."
- "We’ll run a 48-hour canary with the metrics you care about and code-free toggles so your SREs aren’t on the hook for long."

Slide 11 — Appendix: minimal artifact checklist to ship post-atelier
- 1 pager pilot plan (owner, scope, duration, traffic slice)
- Canary template filled + metric thresholds
- One-sentence CFO note with estimated monthly delta
- Ticket created in customer JIRA for fallback coding tasks (link)

Speaker notes / facilitation tips (inside-the-slide cues)
- Keep the first 10 minutes tight — ask two calibration Qs: (1) what is the primary SLO they need? (2) what does a failed pilot cost the business?
- Use the economics micro-sim to pivot from technical to procurement language — tie the numbers to a procurement next step.
- For roleplay, have an engineer play the customer persona and an SE play themselves — this surfaces real staging gaps quickly.

Open questions & next sprints (for the working group)
- We should A/B test a 60m vs 90m atelier to see conversion uplift after three runs
- Instrument a short REDUX: capture top 3 failure modes from each atelier and pipeline them to a weekly ops backlog triage
- Build a lightweight Google Form that captures pilot artifacts automatically and pushes them to our internal pilot-tracker (low effort integration).

Immediate to-dos (owners assigned in session)
- Claire: iterate the canary template with SRE input (due 2025-08-09)
- Tom: prototype the 2-minute economics micro-sim in a Google Sheet (due 2025-08-05)
- Maya: schedule 3 internal practice ateliers and collect failure-mode notes (due 2025-08-20)

Notes to self (rough)
- Keep the deck lean — leave deep audit controls to the Private deployment playbook.
- This atelier should be runnable without privileged infra access; synthetic replay + admin toggles suffice.
- Prioritize building a one-click canary copy/paste snippet for SEs in the Console.

Sample links & references (for distribution pack)
- Pilot checklist template: https://docs.google.com/drive/u/0/fake-pilot-template
- Canary runbook example (internal): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/GTM/Canary+Examples
- Eval harness guide PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/eval-harness/pull/1293

End of deck — feedback welcome.
